prediction_being_tested.what_no_reply_would_establish: Very little on its own. Ten cold emails to busy researchers in August is a weak instrument, and silence is consistent with disinterest, spam filtering, timing, or the question being too obvious to answer. It is the adverse outcome as pre-registered, and it should not be read as evidence that the artifact form is unclaimed.

what_this_record_cannot_establish: That the emails arrived. Delivery was not instrumented; the custodian sent them by hand.
That the two flagged addresses are correct. One domain was completed by the workbench and one was read over an unverified TLS connection; both are recorded above rather than presented as verified.
That the recipients are a representative or well-chosen sample. They were selected by the workbench from web research, in one afternoon, with no prospective rule.

recipient_disclosure.why: Ten researchers were emailed on 2026-08-10 and NONE was told a reply might be published. One later replied 'I wasn't aware you may want to make our private emails public' and asked to be anonymous. The same obligation applies to the other nine whether or not they ever reply, so names and addresses are removed rather than left exposed while a decision is pending.
recipient_disclosure.what_is_kept: count, affiliation, and why each was chosen — which is what makes the 'outreach was done' claim checkable. Identity was never what made it checkable.
recipient_disclosure.how_to_verify: The unredacted list is held by the custodian outside this repository. json.dumps(recipients, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False) over the original hashes to the value above, so the list can be shown to be the one sent without publishing it.
recipient_disclosure.what_this_does_not_fix: Git history retains the unredacted list, and this note does not pretend otherwise. Nine of the ten have still not been asked what they would prefer.
